question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in execute-on-parse mode for streaming tool calls, and should early dispatch require tool-level concurrency-safety metadata first?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the fix changes core runtime scheduling and safety policy rather than repairing a narrowly broken existing contract.

options.title: Design opt-in mode
options.body: Keep the issue open for maintainer design covering scheduling, safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, and proof.

options.title: Block on safety metadata
options.body: Treat the work as dependent on a tool concurrency-safety contract such as the classification proposal in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62962.

options.title: Defer semantics change
options.body: Leave current post-stream execution as the supported behavior if maintainers decide early tool execution is too risky for core now.

recommendation.title: Design opt-in mode
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open for maintainer design covering scheduling, safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, and proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame points to recent work on the central agent-loop file where the scheduling decision would land.
